dedupe_keys.name: northern ireland emergency care waiting times department of health quarterly statistics

description: This series reports the time spent waiting in emergency care departments in Northern Ireland, for new and unplanned review attendances, published quarterly as official statistics by the Department of Health. Figures are given by health and social care trust, by hospital and by type of department (type 1 major emergency departments, type 2 single-specialty and type 3 minor injury units), and measure performance against the ministerial targets such as the four-hour and twelve-hour standards. The department's page lists quarterly releases up to April to June 2026, with a quality report, activity return guidance and a note on the impact of COVID-19; older releases are archived. Tables are free to download as CSV and spreadsheets, and the OpenDataNI catalogue entry marks them as released under the Open Government Licence. Caveats: waiting times start at arrival or triage as defined in the guidance, column layouts change between releases, and ambulance handover times are published separately. Simulation uses: calibrating emergency department capacity and patient flow models, setting baselines for surge and disruption scenarios, and comparing hospital performance before and after extreme events. Related records: the CMS hospital provider data (data-cms-provider-data-hospitals) give comparable United States measures and the Ireland HSE urgent and emergency care report (data-hse-urgent-emergency-care-daily-report) covers the neighbouring system.
